questions.q: Which field is automatically indexed on every MongoDB collection, with no createIndex() call required?
options: _id
All fields are indexed automatically by default
createdAt
No field is indexed automatically — every index must be created explicitly
questions.explain: MongoDB automatically creates an index on _id for every collection when it's created.

questions.q: Given the compound index `{ status: 1, total: -1 }`, which query can it efficiently support?
options: A query filtering on status alone, or on status and total together
A query filtering on total alone, with no status condition
Only queries that filter on neither field
Any query on the collection, regardless of which fields it filters
questions.explain: The leftmost-prefix rule means the index efficiently supports status alone or status+total, but not total in isolation, since total is the second key.

questions.q: What does the ESR rule recommend for ordering fields in a compound index?
options: Equality fields first, then Sort fields, then Range fields
Range fields first, then Equality, then Sort
Alphabetical order of field names
Whichever field was added to the schema first
questions.explain: ESR stands for Equality, Sort, Range — put exact-match filter fields first so the index narrows results before dealing with ranges or ordering.

questions.q: What happens automatically when you create an index on a field whose value is an array?
options: MongoDB creates a multikey index, with one index entry per array element
MongoDB throws an error — array fields cannot be indexed
MongoDB only indexes the first element of the array
MongoDB converts the array field into a separate collection
questions.explain: MongoDB detects the array and automatically builds a multikey index, with an entry for each element, no special declaration required.

questions.q: What is the restriction on compound indexes involving array fields?
options: A compound index can have at most one multikey (array) field
Compound indexes cannot include any array fields at all
Array fields must always be the first key in a compound index
There is no restriction — any number of array fields can be combined
questions.explain: MongoDB disallows compound indexes across two or more array fields because the entry count would explode combinatorially.
